candidate.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12/PDF p.16
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — medication administration routes
candidate.educational_objective: Consider drug and patient factors when determining an appropriate medication route.

options.A: The drug's pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic characteristics, route-specific indications or contraindications, and whether the client can safely use the route
options.B: Only the color of the medication container
options.D: The route should be chosen randomly because route does not influence drug delivery

candidate.rationale: Medication-route selection depends on drug characteristics, desired effect and route-specific advantages/limitations, as well as patient factors such as ability to swallow or tolerate the route.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Medication-route choice should account for drug properties, route indications/contraindications, and patient-specific feasibility.
candidate.source_locator: Route selection — indications/contraindications, pharmacokinetic considerations, and patient feasibility
candidate.source_organization: National Library of Medicine / NCBI Bookshelf (StatPearls)
candidate.stem: When selecting an appropriate route for a medication, which factors should be considered?
